title: Cokernel and image of a morphism of quasi-coherent modules: quasi-coherent, computed on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $q:\mathcal G\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ be the cokernel of $\varphi$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, i.e. the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $U\mapsto\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$, with $q$ the composite of the quotient maps and the sheafification map; and let $\operatorname{Im}\varphi\subseteq\mathcal G$ be the subsheaf of local sections of $\mathcal G$ that are locally in the image of $\varphi$: $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)(W)=\{s\in\mathcal G(W):$ every point of $W$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq W$ with $s|_V\in\varphi_V(\mathcal F(V))\}$. Then: (1) $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$ is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal G$ and equals $\ker q$ (sectionwise kernel), $\varphi$ factors through $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$, and $q$ is an epimorphism with $q\circ\varphi=0$; (2) $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$ are quasi-coherent; (3) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$: $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)(U)=\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$, and $q_U:\mathcal G(U)\to(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)(U)$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$, so that $(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)(U)=\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ as $\mathcal O_X(U)$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas 01IC (tag 01IC), 01IB (tag 01IB), Section 01LA item (5) (tag 01LB); Modules, Lemma 01AH (tag 01AH).

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an affine open. By clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits, $j^*$ is a left adjoint and preserves all colimits, hence it preserves the cokernel of $\varphi$; by clause (2) of that node and the affine-local definition pqf-def-coherent, $j^*\mathcal F$ and $j^*\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent. After choosing $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, the restricted map is therefore a morphism of quasi-coherent modules on $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AJ (tag 01AJ, f^* is left adjoint to f_* and preserves colimits) and Lemma 01BG (tag 01BG, pullback of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent); for an open immersion j, j^* is restriction; the affine-local criterion is pqf-def-coherent.

proof.text: On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, apply clauses (3), (4), and (2) of lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction. Clause (3) identifies each restricted quasi-coherent module with the tilde of its global-sections module; under these identifications $j^*\varphi$ corresponds to the induced $R$-linear map on global sections. Clause (4) says that tilde preserves colimits, so the cokernel is the tilde of the module cokernel; clause (2) identifies its global sections with that module cokernel. Thus $q_U$ is surjective with kernel $\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi(U)=\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas 01IC (tag 01IC, cokernel of M~ -> N~ is the tilde of the module cokernel), 01IB (tag 01IB, affine quasi-coherent equivalence), and 01I7 (tag 01I7, affine tilde/global-sections comparison); the DAG formulation is lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction clauses (2), (3), and (4).

proof.text: Because every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood and quasi-coherence is local by pqf-def-coherent, the cokernel is quasi-coherent on $X$. The kernel of its quotient map is quasi-coherent by lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel, so the image is quasi-coherent once the local-image identification in Step 4 is made.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01LA item (5), tag 01LB (kernels and cokernels of morphisms of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent), together with the affine-neighbourhood criterion pqf-def-coherent.

proof.text: By the sheafified-quotient local-image criterion, a section of $\mathcal G$ lies in the kernel exactly when it is locally in the image of $\varphi$. Thus this kernel is $\operatorname{Im}\varphi$, the map $\varphi$ factors through it, and $q$ is an epimorphism with $q\varphi=0$. The affine formulas of Step 2 give $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)(U)=\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi(U)=\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (tag 01AH, colimits in modules are sheafified presheaf colimits), applied to the quotient presheaf; its kernel consists exactly of sections locally in the image.

lean.statement: theorem quasiCoherent_cokernel_image {X : Scheme.{u}} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] : Mono (Abelian.image.ι φ) ∧ (∀ W : X.Opens, LinearMap.range ((Abelian.image.ι φ).val.app (op W)).hom = LinearMap.ker ((cokernel.π φ).val.app (op W)).hom) ∧ (∀ (W : X.Opens) (s : Γ(G, W)), s ∈ Set.range ((Abelian.image.ι φ).app W) ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∈ W → ∃ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ W), x ∈ V ∧ ∃ t : Γ(F, V), φ.app V t = G.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s) ∧ Abelian.factorThruImage φ ≫ Abelian.image.ι φ = φ ∧ Epi (cokernel.π φ) ∧ φ ≫ cokernel.π φ = 0 ∧ (cokernel φ).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (Abelian.image φ).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (∀ U : X.affineOpens, Set.range ((Abelian.image.ι φ).app U.1) = Set.range (φ.app U.1) ∧ Function.Surjective ((cokernel.π φ).app U.1) ∧ LinearMap.ker ((cokernel.π φ).val.app (op U.1)).hom = LinearMap.range (φ.val.app (op U.1)).hom ∧ ∃ e : (Γ(G, U.1) ⧸ LinearMap.range (φ.val.app (op U.1)).hom) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] Γ(cokernel φ, U.1), ∀ s : Γ(G, U.1), e ((LinearMap.range (φ.val.app (op U.1)).hom).mkQ s) = (cokernel.π φ).app U.1 s)
